A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IDOL and HuGe100K. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across citation and table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction results in Table 2, ablations in Figures 5 and 7, and a 20-participant, 50-case user study in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds consistency measurements, 2K2K reconstruction results, and qualitative diagnostic comparisons in Appendix C.

M1.justification: MVChamp generation, the Sapiens encoder, UV-alignment transformer, Gaussian representation, losses, and skinning procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.1 condenses the skinning explanation; the refined SMPL-X examples test different pose inputs to the existing method.

E1.justification: 2K2K, previously discussed only as related data, becomes an evaluated reconstruction benchmark in v2 Table 4 and Figure 16c. This adds coverage within the existing human-reconstruction task; the training datasets and earlier evaluation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds Zero123 to the multi-view generation comparisons and evaluates TRELLIS plus Make-It-Animatable as a qualitative animation comparator. These supplement the retained baseline groups. GTA and SIFU on 2K2K extend existing comparators to the added benchmark.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces warping-error evaluation over 50 random cases, with THuman2.1 as a reference, and comparisons using original versus refined SMPL-X poses. The 2K2K evaluation states that it follows the existing settings. Original splits, reconstruction metrics, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 16 adds targeted qualitative analyses of SMPL-X pose errors, extreme poses and loose clothing, and topology-related animation artifacts. These are limited case studies supplementing the unchanged MVChamp and IDOL ablations in Figures 5 and 7.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and aggregate user-study percentages without run/seed details, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new 50-case consistency evaluation specifies a test sample, not repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands results with the first quantitative generation-consistency comparison and an additional reconstruction benchmark. Table 3 reports warping errors of 5.38, 7.33, and 10.51 (×10−3) for THuman2.1, MVChamp, and Zero123. Table 4 reports IDOL's 2K2K MSE/PSNR/LPIPS as 0.023/16.688/1.171, outperforming SIFU and GTA there. Figure 16 adds diagnostic findings. Original Table 2 and user-study values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian parameterization, skinning transformations, and training-loss equation are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs; v2 introduces warping error as an evaluation metric without new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and concluding claims retain the same scope: scalable generated human data and fast, photorealistic, animatable single-image reconstruction. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges the lack of dedicated facial identity/expression modeling while removing the limitation about missing human–human and human–object interaction data. Appendix C adds explanations linking bent reconstructions to SMPL-X pose errors and interpreting differences in multi-view consistency and animation topology.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix B retain the architecture specifications, approximately 200,000 sampled vertices, training on 32 H100 GPUs for about one day, and the same optimizer and hyperparameters. The project link is unchanged, with no new code/data availability statement or implementation recipe.

R1.justification: V2 retains the earlier references and adds 16 works, including broader avatar/representation literature and sources for EvalCrafter, TRELLIS, and Make-It-Animatable. A short related-work introduction and supplementary comparisons broaden positioning without redefining the central novelty.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording changes in Sections 4.1, 4.2, 5.2, and 6, adds a short related-work introduction, and expands Appendix C with headed discussions. The overall section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the five-panel Figure 16 and Tables 3–4. The unchanged user-study table moves and becomes Table 5. Earlier figure imagery and table designs are retained, with limited text reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added reconstruction benchmark and quantitative consistency comparison strengthen validation, while the SMPL-X correction examples clarify a practical failure mode. These are useful but limited gains: the new protocols are briefly specified, and the earlier disclosure that interaction data are missing is removed.
